issue_context.title: BUG: Get wrong result when groupby category column with dropna=False
issue_context.body:
I have confirmed this bug exists on the master branch of pandas.

```python
# Your code here
ser = pd.Series([1., 1., 1., 1.])
cat = pd.Categorical(['a', 'b', 'c', np.nan])
print(ser.groupby(cat, dropna=False).sum())
```

```
# output:
a    1.0
b    1.0
c    1.0
dtype: float64
```

#### Expected Output
```
a    1.0
b    1.0
c    1.0
NaN  1.0
dtype: float64
```

comments:
Hey,

have you checked #35646? This looks like a duplicate

It looks different from  #35646 to me -- is specifically about categoricals, and happens with >1 groupby columns?

# Your code here
```ser = pd.Series([1., 1., 1., 1.])

cat = pd.Categorical(['a', 'b', 'c', np.nan])
df = pd.DataFrame({'ser': ser, 'var1': cat, 'var2': cat})
print(df.groupby(['var1', 'var2'], observed=True, dropna=False).sum())

# Same but not categorical
noncat = pd.Series(['a', 'b', 'c', np.nan])
df = pd.DataFrame({'ser': ser, 'var1': noncat, 'var2': noncat})
print(df.groupby(['var1', 'var2'], observed=True, dropna=False).sum())
```

# Output
```           ser
var1 var2     
a    a     1.0
b    b     1.0
c    c     1.0
           ser
var1 var2     
a    a     1.0
b    b     1.0
c    c     1.0
NaN  NaN   1.0
```

# Expected output
```           ser
var1 var2     
a    a     1.0
b    b     1.0
c    c     1.0
NaN  NaN   1.0
           ser
var1 var2     
a    a     1.0
b    b     1.0
c    c     1.0
NaN  NaN   1.0
```
Just a +1 report of hitting this issue, still present on `1.2.0rc0`
Thanks for the report! Further investigations and PRs to fix are welcome.

review_comments: On a 32-bit machine, without the `astype("intp")` numpy will fail (can't safely cast to int32); with it however there could be issues if values exceed the 32bit limitation. This provides a decent speedup, but could be removed if it might cause issues.
Curious what call is trying to cast to int32 before the `astype`, the `bincount` or `!=`?

bincount - I verified this in https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/pull/49652/commits/f3a3ebba9519b5a7eb942c0f060a52a0bed72f5a. The implementation appears to require intp, but I don't know the details as to why. There are a few issues on the NumPy tracker in this regard, but they appear to all be about unsigned integers rather than this case.
Gotcha. Would be good to add a comment here noting that bintcount is requiring the casting to intp.
